thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: high error rate + runtime OOMs observed on-serving-pool-3 — possible autoscale churn (ALERT_ID: autoscale_thrash_7781)
Alex R: seeing a spike in 5xx from the hosted API, graphs show throughput oscillating and many pods in CrashLoopBackOff :/
Priya S: linking quick view: https://grafana.redwood/boards/serving-runtime?panel=autoscale — CPU and GPU utilisation is spiking then dropping repeatedly.
Noah M: stacktrace from one failing pod:
```
2026-03-14T17:12:03Z runtime ERROR: CUDA OOM when allocating 2.1GiB
kv_cache: eviction triggered
terminating with exit code 137
```
Noah M: multiple nodes report ContainerKilled and kubelet OOM kills. Pod lifecycle shows restart count jumping from 0 -> 12 in 10m.
Maya (support): Customers pinging support: a handful of PLG customers reporting intermittent 503s since 17:05 UTC. Quant: ~3% of requests across eu-west region. Triage severity S2 right now but could worsen.
Alex R: suspect autoscaler policy + aggressive downscale. I can see scale-to-zero timer at 30s in the config for low-traffic pools. When pods are evicted, cold-starts hit big memory allocations and push others over memory pressure.
Priya S: action list — (1) disable aggressive downscale for serving-pool-3, (2) pin minReplicas=3, (3) bump gpu-memory-request on runtime pods from 20Gi -> 22Gi as temporary mitigation, (4) cordon & drain any suspected noisy nodes.
Luca (oncall): doing (1) and (2) now. Running:
```
kubectl patch hpa serving-pool-3 -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3}}'
kubectl annotate deploy serving-runtime serving.redwood/scale-disable="true"
```
Luca (oncall): applying memory bump to canary subset (deploy/serving-runtime-canary) first, will rollout if stable.
Noah M: also seeing autoscaler API returning conflicting recommendations — some nodes marked unhealthy then rejoin which triggers scale-up -> pods scheduled -> heavy KV cache warm causing memory transient. Might be a feedback loop from prefix cache warming.
Alex R: to break the loop: disable prefix/KV cache warming on new pods, set warmup=false in config map `runtime-cache-config`.
Priya S: Maya, can you notify affected customers with a brief note? "We're investigating intermittent 503s in eu-west, mitigation in progress, ETA 30-60m".
Maya (support): posted on status.redwood: https://status.redwood/incident/IN-7781 — included workaround: switching to dedicated endpoint if customers need immediate stability.
ops-bot: Deploy job 4872 started for serving-runtime-canary by Luca (oncall).
Luca (oncall): canary rollout succeeded after bump, no OOMs for canary. Rolling to remaining replicas with conservative maxSurge=1.
Alex R: cordoned two nodes that showed repeated OOM kills and evicted pods off them. Node logs show kernel OOM killer invoked around the same timestamps.
Noah M: I'm setting an autoscaler damping window to 5m to prevent rapid down/up cycles: `autoscaler.policy.damping=300s` — applying clusterwide now.
Priya S: Monitoring error rate and latency. Early signs: error rate back to baseline for canary users, overall 5xx down from 3% -> 0.4% in 12m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: oncall escalation to Luca (oncall) acknowledged at 17:29 UTC.
Alex R: recording temporary mitigations for postmortem: bumped mem requests, minReplicas pinned, dampening added, KV-warm disabled, cordoned bad nodes. Need root cause: why KV warm consumes beyond reservation; look into allocator and quantized kernels.
Maya (support): customers updated and ticket queue annotated. No major enterprise customers impacted, flagged PLG tier primarily.
Priya S: handoff: I'm out at 18:00 UTC — handing off incident lead to Luca. Handoff notes: watch for re-flare after uncordon; do not revert damping or minReplicas until 2h stable. Postmortem owner: Priya S.
Luca (oncall): taking lead. Remaining tasks for next shift: (A) run memory profiler on runtime to capture allocation spikes, (B) run node-level repro on a drained node, (C) evaluate longer-term autoscale policy changes (min windows, safe-capacity buffers). I'll keep support in the loop.
Maya (support): prepping customer follow-ups with incident timeline and ETA for postmortem.
Noah M: created temporary debug job to attach to a restarted pod and capture `dmesg` + `nvidia-smi` output during warmup. Link: https://internal.redwood/debug/attach/3456
Luca (oncall): uncordoning one node now after we verified stability on others. Will watch for 10m.
Priya S: leaving Slack thread; followup: assign postmortem to Priya S and Noah M for allocator analysis.
Luca (oncall): 17:58 UTC — stability check: 10m window with no new OOMs, error rate stable. Closing incident channel in 30m, will open postmortem doc and link back here.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied — downgraded severity to S3 at 18:05 UTC.
Maya (support): support notes saved to ticket #SR-9087. Will update customers when PM/SE review postmortem.
ops-bot: Reminder: please fill the incident form: https://docs.redwood/incidents/new — owner: Priya S, severity: S2 (initial)/S3 (mitigated).
Luca (oncall): handoff complete to next oncall @Alex R for final checks, I'm going offline soon. If anything flares, page me.
Priya S: postmortem stub created: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/IN-7781 — initial hypothesis: autoscaler downscale + KV warm + memory overcommit -> feedback loop.
Alex R: noted. Thanks team. I'll follow up on a corrective action to add safety buffer to node capacity and tune warmup heuristics. :thumbsup:
